question_text: Why is the true coelom considered a secondary body cavity?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The primary cavity
steps.why: The words primary and secondary are about ORDER in development, so the answer has to name the cavity that comes first.
common_mistakes: Writing about the adult animal only. Primary and secondary refer to the order in which the cavities appear in the embryo.
steps.memory_tip: First cavity is the blastocoel. Anything that comes after it is secondary.
steps.margin_note: Name the blastocoel and call it the primary cavity. Two lines.
lines: In the developing embryo the first cavity to
The blastocoel is therefore the primary body

steps.label: Why the coelom is secondary
steps.why: The true coelom is not the first cavity but a second one cut out of the mesoderm, and its mesodermal origin is what separates it from the blastocoel.
common_mistakes: Writing that secondary means less important. It means later in development.
Leaving out mesoderm. The true coelom is a cavity inside the mesoderm, and that is what makes it new.
steps.memory_tip: Blastocoel first, coelom second: the coelom is cut out of the mesoderm afterwards.
steps.margin_note: State that the coelom forms later, inside the mesoderm. That is the whole answer.

lines.text: Forms after the blastocoel, so it is second

lines: Later the blastocoel is replaced by a new
cavity that forms within the mesoderm.
This mesodermal cavity is the true coelom.
Because it appears after the primary cavity,
the true coelom is called the secondary body

insider_note: The examiner is looking for two words in order — blastocoel first, mesoderm second; a card that names only the coelom scores half.
